machine.loadavg_note: this repository's CI machine is shared; a load average above the cpu count means the milliseconds below are inflated by other work on the box

world.note: START_WORLD enables work by default and employs every citizen with a workplace

registration.note: a fresh WorkRuntime on a work:false world, so every registry is cold; registry(bid) builds the SmartObjectRegistry and the RoomGraph and internally calls World.interior_descriptor(bid), whose cost is measured separately on the same buildings

task_selection.note: _select_work_task is side-effecting (reservations, events), so it is timed in place on a live world rather than replayed on a copy

reservations.note: a standalone ledger over one real building's objects, cid 0..999

held_by_scan.note: held_by(cid) scans every held object; release(cid) uses it

0900.scenario: 09:00 shift start, workers walking to stations

navigation.note: route() is BFS over the doorway graph; the pairs are the centres of every room pair (capped), which is the worst case a walk can ask for

focus.note: the work runtime never reads focus_xy or the LOD band — there is no reference to either anywhere in asphodel/smart — so a NEAR workplace runs exactly the same Python as a FAR one. The measured work delta of 0.374 ms/game-minute is machine noise plus the mobility band change (far bands {'route_simulated': 297}, near bands {'route_simulated': 294, 'physical': 3}); mobility freezes citizens into ABSTRACT only beyond max_active=1024 and this city registers 297, so nothing froze either way. The Godot-side cost of embodying a NEAR worker is measured by the in-engine gate, not here.

near_embodiment.reason: materialising interior worker bodies, their station animations and the MOBILITY_REPORT rows they add is Godot-side cost; this tool measures the Python authority only

full_hour_0700_0800.note: one timed game minute at a time; the departure peak is a mobility route-planning spike, not a work-runtime cost

outbreak_plus_work.scenario: outbreak (classic_zombie, data-driven index case) + work, seeded 05:00, measured 11:00-11:20

worker_heavy.scenario: worker-heavy 11:00 — every citizen employed at the 5 largest workplaces
worker_heavy.caveat: employment alone does not create work sessions: WorkRuntime only opens a worker session when the TripExecutor has actually delivered the citizen into emp.workplace_id with activity 'work' (smart/runtime.py:234), and the mobility runtime still routes everyone to the workplace in their own bundle profile. This scenario therefore measures a maximal employment table and a maximal per-workplace object/registry load, not 297 simultaneous worker sessions.

profile.note: cProfile inflates absolute cost; read the shares, not the milliseconds. The unprofiled cost of the same window is the 'advance' rows above.

hotspots.scaling: per registered citizen per 1 s substep — the `for cid in sorted(execs)` loop has no skip list, so it is O(citizens) x 60 per game minute even when nobody is working; the sorted() itself is O(n log n) per substep
per registered citizen per 1 s substep — the mobility baseline this milestone adds to; citizens settled inside a building are skipped (embodied/runtime.py:464-471)
per citizen per substep per caller — mobility and work each ask independently
per citizen per substep per caller
per citizen currently walking to an object, per 1 s substep

per registered citizen per 1 s substep (60 per game minute), whether or not that citizen is anywhere near a building — WorkRuntime._substep classifies every executor every substep (smart/runtime.py:202-223)
per citizen with an open session per substep, gated by a.next_s wake scheduling
per walking citizen per substep x rooms in the building (linear scan over every room rectangle)
per game minute: 60 substeps x O(citizens)
per task selection x objects in the workplace

budget.note: at 24x one game minute is 2.5 s of real time (2500 ms). The heaviest measured game-minute (52.826 ms, 297 citizens) uses 2.11% of it; the work runtime is 16.99 ms of that. The 07:00-08:00 hour, measured minute by minute, averages 545.39 ms and peaks at 10886.757 ms in one game minute (10879.351 ms of it mobility route planning), 3 minute(s) of that hour over budget. Registration is a one-off 1257 ms for every workplace and home in the city, paid lazily per building on first entry.
